INTRODUCTIONM
Microprocessors are used everywhere: from computers, televisions and microwaves, to cars, stereos and even sewing machines.
Today, microprocessors aid in the development of cars, electronic circuits, bridges and more. They provide the power to analyze every little detail in short amounts of time.
In business, microprocessors aid in keeping track of large inventories or an employee database. Microprocessors perform thousands of tedious tasks in small amounts of time.
In industry, microprocessors are sometimes called microcontrollers, and are used in automated machinery and robotics, enhancing performance to maximize production.
Microprocessors have proven their usefulness in nearly all aspects of our lives. They can be found in many electronic games, automatic bank tellers and cash registers.
They can be found at home, in VCR's, small appliances, microwave ovens and, of course, personal computers.

A microprocessor system is made up of five basic parts: the input, the control, the memory, the arithmetic logic unit and the output.
Input is the information provided to the microprocessor. The most common input device is the keyboard. Other input devices include tapes, hard and floppy disks, mouse and other devices.ces.
Output is the information generated by the microprocessor. We receive the microprocessor's output in many ways. The most common output devices are the video screen and printers.
The Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) is the device which performs all the math and logic functions for the microprocessor.
The memory section contains all the data used by the system. This includes both instructions and information.
The control section regulates the movement of data and the processing of data at the inputs and outputs.

The control unit also activates the ALU, allowing the modified data to be returned to memory.

You have seen data travel from one section of the microprocessor to another. Data is transferred from one section to another using a system of wires called buses.to connect the sections. Data is transferred from one section to another on these buses.........
The data bus carries data between the main sections of the system as controlled by the microprocessor.
The address bus selects a memory location or an input/output device.
This allows the memory or input/output device to place data on or take data from the data bus.
The control bus carries various signals from the microprocessor that coordinate operations.
These signals control the other devices and allow the CPU to know if data is being received or sent.
